title: Letter 5 — The Marks of a Living Faith
attribution_note: Letter 5 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance. Part of the four-letter treatise On Faith (Letters 2–5); see Letter 2's note.

sections.heading: How faith is known by its fruit

pairs.en: You ask: what are the marks of a living faith in a man?

I answer. A living faith is known by its works, as a tree by its fruit. We call that tree good which bears good fruit. And the fruit comes forth from within the tree, from its root and sap, for such as the root and sap of a tree are, such also is its fruit: if the root and sap in a tree are good, its fruit is good too. So also faith is known by good works, coming forth from within, from the heart, without any hypocrisy. And as clear streams flow from a clear spring, so good works proceed and appear from a heart purified by holy faith. And as a vessel filled with balsam, or holding even some part of it, gives off a good fragrance, so the human heart, filled with the spiritual balsam of holy faith, gives off the good fragrance of deeds pleasing to God and useful to men.
The marks of a living faith, then, are these:

sections.heading: The marks of a living faith

pairs.en: 1) To honour from the heart the God whom faith sees, and to whom it clings as a small child to its mother, in the manner described in His holy word — that is, not in matter and outward form only, but *“in spirit and in truth,”* since God Himself *“is a Spirit”* [John 4:24] — and to honour Him alone above all the world, for the whole world is as nothing before Him; and to acknowledge and call Him from the heart your own God, though He is God of all, just as He is called the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, for the sake of their faith, though He is God of all nations. [Exodus 3:6, 15–16; Mark 12:26] From this will follow true and sincere obedience and submission to Him. For if He is your God, then, as your God, He must be obeyed, and His will and command carried out, just as you obey your father because he is your father.

2) To guard against every sin without hypocrisy, because He is offended by every sin. You do not wish to offend your father in anything, and dare not do anything unseemly before him; much less ought you to offend your God, who is everywhere and sees everything, or do anything before Him that is displeasing to Him. Every sin is contrary to the Christian faith, and so faith fights against every sin. Faith loves to rest in a clean conscience, and cannot exist without a clean conscience. So the holy apostle wrote: *“Holding faith, and a good conscience; which some having put away concerning faith have made shipwreck.”* [1 Timothy 1:19] To know God and honour Him on the one hand, but on the other to sin against conscience, and so to offend and provoke God — this is a plain contradiction. Consider this carefully, and you will discover this truth for yourself.

3) To thank Him from the heart for all the kindnesses shown and still being shown to us, which are past all number, so that we cannot live even a minute without His kindnesses. We are enclosed in His kindnesses, and surrounded by them; we are indebted to Him for our body, our soul, our breath, and our whole being, and everything else.
4) To call upon God from the heart, without hypocrisy, and in every need to flee to Him alone, and ask His help.

As a small child runs to its mother, and stretches out its hands, and asks her for protection and everything else, and knows nothing besides its mother, so faith clings to God alone, and asks everything of Him, and in its needs knows no one but God. For faith knows that God alone can do all things, and that hope in Him is sure, while every other hope, apart from Him, is unsure and vain.

5) To honour the incarnation of the Son of God, and all His most precious dispensation, as the one source of our salvation, as a great and precious thing, above all else. For faith sees that, as great and beyond human understanding as this work of God's goodness is, so greatly must it be honoured and worshipped — with all humility and thanksgiving.

6) To know no other Mediator, for obtaining freedom from sin, the devil, hell and every misery and wretchedness, and for obtaining eternal life with eternal glory, than Jesus Christ alone. For He alone is the Redeemer and Saviour of the whole world, and therefore to Him alone must be ascribed the beginning, the middle and the end of eternal salvation. Faith sees that all its spiritual blessedness consists in Jesus Christ alone. He is for it *“wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption.”* [1 Corinthians 1:30] Hoping in this all-powerful Redeemer, Saviour, Helper and Defender, it grows bold and triumphs over all its enemies, and comforts itself thereby in all the temptations brought upon it by the devil and his evil servants, and cries out with the preacher of the faith: *“If God be for us, who can be against us?”* [Romans 8:31]

7) A plain sign of a living faith is to follow Christ, bearing one's own cross. For the faithful soul is joined to Christ, as a bride to the bridegroom and as a body to its head, and therefore wishes to be with Him without separation, both in suffering and in glorification, as a bride with the bridegroom and a body with its head. For it is not fitting that a bride should be parted from the bridegroom, nor a body from its head. Of this the apostle wrote: *“Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow His steps”* [1 Peter 2:21]; and again: *“Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus,”* and the rest. [Philippians 2:5] And the Lord Himself says: *“I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.”* [John 13:15]

8) Not to set the heart upon anything in this world — neither upon riches, nor honour, nor glory, nor its other treasures — but always to look toward the future and eternal blessings, to think upon them, to desire them, and to find comfort in them; *“to set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth; to seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God,”* as the apostle teaches. [Colossians 3:1–2] For living faith comes from heaven, and therefore stirs up and moves the faithful soul toward heaven. And the faithful soul sees that it is on a road and a journey in this world, and therefore *“hath here no continuing city, but seeketh one to come, whose builder and maker is God.”* [Hebrews 13:14; 11:10] From this we see, in the Psalms, the desires and sighings of faithful souls, which they lift up toward their heavenly fatherland and its blessings, as they journey through this world as through a foreign land.

9) Faith has the fear of God, and also spiritual joy and gladness. And these work by turns in the faithful soul: now it feels fear and trembling, now it feels joy and gladness. Sometimes faith hides itself, and then the soul fears and trembles. Sometimes it shows itself, and then the soul is comforted, rejoices, is glad, and exults in spirit.

10) Faith is humble, patient, meek, loving, merciful, gracious, peaceable, and the rest. For where faith is, there also is the grace of the Holy Spirit, which produces all this in the faithful soul. Of this the apostle speaks to every Christian: *“Show me thy faith by thy works,”* as Abraham showed his faith by his works. [James 2:18–21] Read Holy Scripture, and especially the Psalms, in which the workings of a living faith are vividly portrayed. For faith, being a spiritual gift, is known by the spiritual workings that take place in the heart. We shall then know what faith is, when we feel its workings in the heart — which I heartily desire, both for myself and for you.
